passage:
With the rise of pop music, jazz, and electronic music, both opera and classical music started to fade away from the public eye. Some people are beginning to wonder whether opera and classical music are still relevant to the modern world of music. Granted, you will not typically see today's teenagers lending their ears to Bach anytime soon, but there are some major indicators that both opera and classical music are now still quite alive.

The most major indicator of classical music's importance in society today is the fact that much of the popular music that is currently being produced uses similar beats, harmonies, and melodies(旋律) as those that were used in some of classical music's best works. Even so, it can be difficult for those who do not study music theory to see this as an indicator, since it is subtle and just shows the impact symphonic(交响乐的) orchestras have had on society's taste in music.

A better example for the relevance of opera and classical music can be seen in the invention of the rock opera. Opera, in its simplest definition, is telling a story using music as its form. The art of telling a story using music has not faded in the least bit. In fact, sometimes actual orchestras are used for major parts of the opera itself. Some of the world's greatest hits have been parts of rock operas.

Fans of classical music can also tell you that there are few types of music that are more expressive. So, it should come as no surprise to anyone that classical music pieces are still used as background music in modern movies. Symphonic orchestra compositions have also been created solely for the purpose of being included in major motion pictures. These are often very well received amongst mainstream music fans.

Classical music and opera are the very foundation of what our modern music is based upon. Considering the huge impact they have had on our current society, it is without doubt that we can expect them to continue to remain important for centuries to come.
passage_translation: 随着流行音乐、爵士乐和电子音乐的兴起,歌剧和古典音乐都开始从公众视野中淡出。一些人开始疑惑歌剧和古典音乐在现代音乐世界中是否仍然具有相关性。诚然,你通常不会看到今天的青少年很快就会去聆听Bach的作品,但有一些重要迹象表明歌剧和古典音乐现在仍然相当活跃。
古典音乐在当今社会重要性的最主要标志是,目前制作的大量流行音乐使用了与古典音乐一些最佳作品中所使用的相似的节拍、和声和旋律。即便如此,对于那些不研究音乐理论的人来说,可能很难将此视为一个标志,因为它是微妙的,只是显示了交响乐团对社会音乐品味产生的影响。
歌剧和古典音乐相关性的一个更好例子可以从摇滚歌剧的发明中看到。歌剧,用最简单的定义来说,就是用音乐作为形式来讲述故事。用音乐讲述故事的艺术丝毫没有消退。事实上,有时真正的管弦乐队会被用于歌剧本身的主要部分。世界上一些最伟大的热门歌曲都是摇滚歌剧的组成部分。
古典音乐的爱好者也会告诉你,很少有音乐类型比古典音乐更具表现力。因此,古典音乐作品仍被用作现代电影的背景音乐,这对任何人来说都不应感到意外。交响乐团作品也被专门创作用于收录在重要电影作品中。这些作品通常在主流音乐爱好者中受到很好的评价。
古典音乐和歌剧是我们现代音乐所基于的根基。考虑到它们对我们当前社会产生的巨大影响,毫无疑问我们可以期待它们在未来几个世纪中继续保持重要地位。

passage:
Our society places a high value on physical beauty. Americans spend an average of over $722 each year on their appearance. One in ten Americans has tried to look like a star.

There's nothing wrong with trying to look our best, but excessive focus on physical appearance misses the soulful aspects of what it means to be beautiful. Trying to look like the magazine pictures can take us on a long ride away from what beauty is really about.

Many of us spend far too much time, energy, and money trying to polish an image of what we think will bring attention, love, and connection. In the process, we may fail to attend to ourselves in a way that would move us toward deeper intimacy, fulfillment, and meaning.

It may sound trite(老生常谈的), but beauty is only skin deep; it's not what brings love toward us. Just read about the latest Hollywood starlets whose seeming love turns into resentment and bitter court battles.

Outer beauty can be as much of a curse as a blessing. We may develop a habit of being so focused on maintaining a perfect appearance that we never cultivate the inner qualities necessary to sustain and deepen intimacy and connection. As I describe in my book, The Authentic Heart, it is the courage to be authentic that connects us in a deeper way.

While our initial attraction may be based, in part, on physical chemistry, it is the meeting of our inner worlds that creates the lasting intimacy and spiritual connection for which we long. If we redirect our attention toward cultivating inner qualities, we might find a magnetic attraction that moves us from something superficial to something that connects us to our depths.

The path toward cultivating inner beauty is really simple. But what is simple is not always easy. Not everyone will see us and appreciate us as we take the courageous risk to allow ourselves to be seen as we really are. But if they don't, it is their loss, not ours. Eventually we'll find those compatible souls who appreciate us as we are.
passage_translation: 我们的社会高度重视外在美。美国人平均每年在外表上花费超过722美元。每十个美国人中就有一个试图让自己看起来像明星。
努力让自己看起来最好并没有什么错,但过度关注外表会忽略美的真正含义中那些关乎灵魂的方面。试图看起来像杂志照片中的样子可能会让我们远离美的真正意义。
我们中的许多人花费了太多时间、精力和金钱来打磨一个我们认为能带来关注、爱和联系的形象。在这个过程中,我们可能无法以一种能让我们走向更深层次的亲密、满足和意义的方式来关注自己。
这可能听起来老生常谈,但美只是肤浅的;它不是给我们带来爱的东西。只需读读好莱坞最新明星们的故事,她们看似的爱情变成了怨恨和激烈的法庭争斗。
外在美既可能是诅咒也可能是祝福。我们可能养成一种习惯,过于专注于保持完美的外表,以至于从未培养维持和深化亲密关系和联系所必需的内在品质。正如我在《真实的心》一书中所描述的,正是真实的勇气以更深刻的方式将我们联系在一起。
虽然我们最初的吸引力可能部分基于身体上的化学反应,但正是我们内心世界的相遇创造了我们渴望的持久亲密和精神联系。如果我们将注意力转向培养内在品质,我们可能会发现一种磁性吸引力,使我们从肤浅的东西走向与我们内心深处相连的东西。
培养内在美的道路其实很简单。但简单的事情并不总是容易的。当我们冒着勇敢的风险让自己以真实的样子被看见时,不是每个人都会看到我们并欣赏我们。但如果他们不欣赏,那是他们的损失,而不是我们的。最终我们会找到那些欣赏真实的我们的志同道合的灵魂。

passage:
Plant-based meats are coming soon to a dinner table near you, but do they deserve a spot on your plate? If you tried a vegetable burger years ago and dismissed it as rubbery and flavorless, it's a good time to give meatless meat another chance. Newer varieties imitate the look, flavor, and texture of meat. Analysts don't expect the meat-free movement to slow anytime soon; a 2021 report predicts the market will skyrocket to $74 billion by 2030—a 957 percent surge.

Plant-based meats are no longer just for vegetarians. Companies such as Impossible Foods and Beyond Meat—the current superstars of the alternative protein sector—are pursuing consumers who enjoy meat but want to reduce their meat consumption for animal rights, health, or environmental reasons. So far, it's a winning strategy: More than nine out of ten consumers who buy Beyond Burger and Impossible Foods products also eat meat.

Many vegetarians don't actually care for food that resembles meat. When reporter Joan Solsman, a longtime vegetarian, tried a dish from Impossible Foods, she felt so sick that she couldn't finish it. "Maybe the best sign that Impossible Foods has cracked the code to realistic fake meat is that I couldn't stand to take another bite," she wrote.

Meatless meats are generally a healthier choice than beef because they are cholesterol-free, plus they're a good source of vitamins, minerals, protein, and fiber.

If meatless meat can help you stick to a plant-based diet, that in itself can lead to better health. Not only has red meat been linked to cancer, but studies show that people who ditch meat have lower blood pressure, lower average blood sugar, and lower cholesterol levels.

However, just because it's plant-based doesn't mean it's health food. Most imitation meats are highly processed and contain high amounts of sodium(钠) compared to traditional beef.

These new generations of alternate meat get all the attention, but don't forget about whole grains and vegetables. Beans are an especially excellent protein substitute. They're nutritious, inexpensive, and far more sustainable than any of the processed meatless substitutes on the market today.
passage_translation: 植物基肉类即将出现在你附近的餐桌上,但它们值得在你的盘子里占有一席之地吗?如果你几年前尝试过蔬菜汉堡并认为它像橡胶一样且毫无味道,现在是再给无肉肉类一次机会的好时机。较新的品种模仿了肉类的外观、风味和质地。分析师预计无肉运动不会很快放缓;2021年的一份报告预测,到2030年该市场将飙升至740亿美元——增长957%。
植物基肉类不再只是素食主义者的选择。Impossible Foods和Beyond Meat等公司——目前替代蛋白质领域的超级明星——正在追求那些喜欢肉类但出于动物权利、健康或环境原因想要减少肉类消费的消费者。到目前为止,这是一个成功的策略:购买Beyond Burger和Impossible Foods产品的消费者中,超过十分之九的人也吃肉。
许多素食主义者实际上并不喜欢类似肉类的食物。当记者Joan Solsman——一位长期素食主义者——尝试Impossible Foods的一道菜时,她感到非常恶心以至于无法吃完。她写道:"也许Impossible Foods已经破解了逼真假肉密码的最好标志就是我无法再咬一口。"
无肉肉类通常比牛肉更健康,因为它们不含胆固醇,而且是维生素、矿物质、蛋白质和纤维的良好来源。
如果无肉肉类可以帮助你坚持植物性饮食,那本身就能带来更好的健康。红肉不仅与癌症有关,而且研究表明,不吃肉的人血压更低、平均血糖更低、胆固醇水平也更低。
然而,仅仅因为它是植物基的并不意味着它是健康食品。与传统牛肉相比,大多数仿制肉类都经过高度加工,并含有大量钠。
这些新一代替代肉类获得了所有关注,但不要忘记全谷物和蔬菜。豆类是特别优秀的蛋白质替代品。它们营养丰富、价格低廉,而且比当今市场上任何加工过的无肉替代品都更可持续。

passage:
All living organisms on Earth are exposed to a 24-hour day-night cycle. This cycle is the reason why people rest at night and are active during the day. Consequently, all human body functions also follow this daily rhythm, and the timing of behaviors like exercise or food intake can significantly influence your health. For example, eating at night can lead to weight gain over time because food intake at night leads to increased fat storage.

Many drug targets in the body follow a 24-hour cycle, too. This means that the specific proteins a drug is designed to modify can react differently to the medicine over the course of a 24-hour time period. Because how the body responds to a drug can differ depending on the time it is taken, it logically follows that taking medicines at specific times could help increase their effectiveness and reduce unwanted side effects.

When doctors prescribe medicine for people, they rarely consider the best time to take it. There are two main reasons for that oversight. First, many physicians are not aware that some drugs work better during a specific time of the day. And second, most drugs have not been studied for possible different effects during a 24-hour cycle. Therefore, patients are directed to take most drugs during the morning or evening primarily to ensure compliance.

Over 50 years ago, researchers found that the cholesterol drug simvastatin is more effective at lowering cholesterol levels when taken at night rather than during the day. This is because the liver enzyme(酶) these drugs target is more active at night.

Taking medicine at the wrong time can even cause harm. My colleagues and I wondered whether midazolam, the most common sedative(镇静剂) used in surgical procedures worldwide, might interfere with the internal clock that protects the heart at night. Currently, there are no guidelines regarding when midazolam should be administered.

More research is needed to determine the best times to administer treatments for different diseases. I believe taking drug timing into account could help make treatments more effective and help more people worldwide.
passage_translation: 地球上所有生物都暴露在24小时昼夜循环之中。这种循环是人们夜间休息、白天活动的原因。因此,所有人体功能也遵循这一日常节律,而运动或进食等行为的时间安排可以显著影响您的健康。例如,夜间进食会随着时间推移导致体重增加,因为夜间摄入食物会导致脂肪储存增加。
体内许多药物靶点也遵循24小时周期。这意味着药物旨在修饰的特定蛋白质在24小时时间段内对药物的反应可能有所不同。由于身体对药物的反应会因服药时间而异,因此合乎逻辑的是,在特定时间服药可能有助于提高药效并减少不良副作用。
当医生为患者开药时,他们很少考虑最佳服药时间。这种疏忽有两个主要原因。首先,许多医生不知道某些药物在一天中的特定时间效果更好。其次,大多数药物尚未就24小时周期内可能产生的不同效果进行研究。因此,患者被指示在早晨或晚上服用大多数药物,主要是为了确保依从性。
50多年前,研究人员发现降胆固醇药物辛伐他汀在夜间服用比白天服用更能有效降低胆固醇水平。这是因为这些药物针对的肝酶在夜间更为活跃。
在错误的时间服药甚至可能造成伤害。我和同事们想知道咪达唑仑——全球外科手术中最常用的镇静剂——是否会干扰夜间保护心脏的内部时钟。目前,关于何时应给予咪达唑仑尚无指南。
需要更多研究来确定针对不同疾病实施治疗的最佳时间。我相信将药物给药时间纳入考虑可以帮助使治疗更有效,并帮助全世界更多的人。

passage:
Katharine Abraham, an economics professor, was chatting with her hairdresser(理发师) about retirement plans. The economist said she plans to continue working because she wants to. The hairdresser agreed but for a different reason: She needs the money.

Both scenarios(情况) are contributing to a big increase in the number of people in the U.S. working into their 70s. Over the past 20 years, the share of Americans working in their 70s has risen from less than 10% to nearly 15%.

In addition to people being healthier and living much longer, economists say that a combination of financial considerations such as years of slow rise in real wages and a shift away from traditional pensions in the private sector are some of the reasons people delay retirement. The decline of manufacturing and the increase in the number of people working in less labor-intensive occupations also has contributed to the trend, says Abraham, who researches work and retirement decisions of older Americans.

"Which matters more depends on what your history up until that point has been in the type of work you're doing," Abraham says.

The overall trend is hitting Americans of all different levels of educational attainment, although the percentages vary by category. The share of Americans with bachelor's degrees who were working into their 70s reached nearly 20% in 2018. For those with a high school degree or less, the proportion of those working in their 70s had risen to around 10%, while those with some college education were in the middle at around 15%.

Martin Neil Baily, an economist who is leading a research project on retirement security, notes that quitting a career can lead to feelings of isolation and loneliness, particularly for men. He suggests that many college-educated workers are choosing to stay in the labor force more for social benefits than for financial reasons. They're also more likely to be in professional occupations where they tend to enjoy their work more.

Workers in more physical jobs, meanwhile, may be more likely to look forward to retiring, Baily says, suggesting those who stay on are more likely doing so for financial reasons.
passage_translation: 经济学教授Katharine Abraham正在与她的理发师闲聊退休计划。这位经济学家说她计划继续工作，因为她想这样做。理发师表示同意，但原因不同：她需要钱。
这两种情况都促使美国70多岁仍在工作的人数大幅增加。在过去20年里，70多岁仍在工作的美国人比例已从不到10%上升到近15%。
除了人们更健康、寿命更长之外，经济学家表示，实际工资多年缓慢增长以及私营部门传统养老金制度的转变等一系列财务因素，是人们推迟退休的部分原因。制造业的衰落和从事劳动密集程度较低职业的人数增加也促成了这一趋势，研究美国老年人工作和退休决策的Abraham说。
Abraham说："哪个因素更重要取决于你在那之前从事的工作类型的历史。"
这一总体趋势正影响着所有不同教育程度的美国人，尽管各类别的百分比有所不同。拥有学士学位的美国人中，在70多岁仍在工作的比例在2018年达到近20%。对于那些拥有高中或更低学历的人，70多岁仍在工作的比例已上升至约10%,而那些受过一些大学教育的人则处于中间水平，约为15%。
正在领导一项退休保障研究项目的经济学家Martin Neil Baily指出，结束职业生涯可能会导致孤立感和孤独感，尤其是对男性而言。他认为，许多受过大学教育的工作者选择留在劳动力市场更多是为了社交利益而非经济原因。他们也更有可能从事专业职业，往往更享受自己的工作。
与此同时,从事体力工作的工作者可能更倾向于期待退休，Baily说，这表明那些继续工作的人更有可能是出于经济原因。

passage:
Junk food is now a staple of many Americans' diets. Advertising campaigns from the snack food companies, often featuring sports stars, send the message that we can neutralize any negative effects of consuming their products simply by getting more physical exercise. But recent studies show a lack of exercise is not to blame for rising obesity rates. Bad diets are.

Interventions(干预) to help reduce junk food consumption are especially important for children and teenagers. Prevention is better than cure because obesity is so difficult to treat. Unfortunately, while health education has shown some success among young children, teens have been harder to reach.

Now a large-scale study has tried an innovative approach to change teenagers' attitudes towards healthy eating, and the results are promising. The researchers argued that previous interventions have probably been unsuccessful because of a major flaw: they focused on a future, healthier you and assumed that this would be enough motivation for teenagers. In contrast, the new intervention cleverly exploits teenagers' instinct for rebelliousness and autonomy, and the value they place on social justice.

To do this, researchers had students read an article on the food industry. It revealed a secret about the manipulative and deceptive strategies used to make junk food more addictive and characterize the products as healthy. The article also explained how advertising campaigns specifically target very young and poor people, causing harm for these vulnerable groups. Afterwards, the participants read a fictional survey of teens who wanted to "fight back against the companies by buying and eating less processed food"

After the intervention, participants associated healthy eating with autonomy and social justice. The teenagers also rated healthy eating as being more appealing. Importantly, there were also some promising effects of the new intervention on actual behavior. A day later the students were offered a choice of snacks and drinks in a seemingly unrelated context. The teens chose healthy snacks and drinks (such as fruit or water) more often over unhealthy options (like biscuits and soda). Apparently associating a healthy diet with teenagers' own values seems to be a promising avenue to prevent obesity.
passage_translation: 垃圾食品现在已成为许多美国人饮食的主要组成部分。零食公司的广告宣传活动常常以体育明星为代言人,传递这样一种信息:我们可以仅仅通过增加体育锻炼来抵消食用其产品的任何负面影响。但最近的研究表明,缺乏锻炼并不是肥胖率上升的罪魁祸首。不良饮食才是。
帮助减少垃圾食品消费的干预措施对儿童和青少年尤为重要。预防胜于治疗,因为肥胖症非常难以治疗。不幸的是,尽管健康教育在幼儿中取得了一些成功,但青少年却更难触及。
现在,一项大规模研究尝试了一种创新方法来改变青少年对健康饮食的态度,结果令人鼓舞。研究人员认为,以往的干预措施可能不成功是因为存在一个重大缺陷:它们关注的是未来更健康的你,并假定这足以激励青少年。相比之下,新的干预措施巧妙地利用了青少年的叛逆和自主本能,以及他们对社会公正的重视。
为此,研究人员让学生阅读一篇关于食品行业的文章。文章揭示了一个秘密,即用于使垃圾食品更容易上瘾并将产品标榜为健康食品的操纵性和欺骗性策略。文章还解释了广告宣传活动如何专门针对非常年幼和贫困的人群,对这些弱势群体造成伤害。之后,参与者阅读了一份虚构的青少年调查,这些青少年想要"通过少购买和少食用加工食品来反击这些公司"。
干预之后,参与者将健康饮食与自主和社会公正联系起来。青少年还认为健康饮食更具吸引力。重要的是,新的干预措施对实际行为也产生了一些令人鼓舞的影响。一天后,学生们在一个看似无关的情境中被提供零食和饮料的选择。青少年更多地选择健康的零食和饮料(如水果或水),而不是不健康的选项(如饼干和苏打水)。显然,将健康饮食与青少年自身的价值观联系起来似乎是预防肥胖的一个有希望的途径。

passage:
Adults dream during REM (rapid eye movement) sleep and infants have loads of REM. So, it might be fair to assume that babies have tons of dreams.

But scientists believe REM serves a completely different purpose for newborns and infants than dreaming. When babies are in REM, it allows their brain to develop pathways, connections, and eventually, learn languages.

Since your baby doesn't dream at this stage of brain development, it's safe to assume babies do not have nightmares, either. Nightmares stem from exposure to trauma(创伤), an overactive imagination, and the normal stresses of everyday life.

Are you wondering, what do babies dream about? Good question, but the answer is nothing! So, when do babies start dreaming? The general consensus is that they start dreaming around the age of two. Psychologist David Foulkes studies children (from very small kids to teens) to bring the secrets of their dreams to the light of day. In his lab, he lets kids fall asleep and then wakes them 3 times a night and asks them to describe what they recall.

Foulkes' findings are unsurprising. Basically, little kids have little dreams. But exactly what kids see while dreaming depends on their age. As children develop and grow, their dreams do too.

Dreams of very small kids are usually just snapshots(快照), looking much more like a slideshow than a movie, when compared to the dreams of adults. They heavily feature animals and other familiar sights, like images of people eating. According to Foulkes, "Children's dream life…seems to be similar to their waking imagination and narration." Kids ages 5 – 9 begin seeing moving images and characters in action. Dreams now include multiple events strung together, one after the other. They also start developing greater ability to remember dreams. Still, that's not always the case: When roused during REM sleep, 25% of the kids in Foulkes' studies had no recollection of dreaming, a trend that continues through age 9.

So, if your baby seems to be in a stressful state while sleeping or is upset upon waking, there may be other factors at play.
passage_translation: 成年人在REM（快速眼动）睡眠期间做梦，而婴儿有大量的REM睡眠。因此，可以合理地假设婴儿有很多梦。
但科学家认为，REM对新生儿和婴儿的作用与做梦完全不同。当婴儿处于REM状态时,它使他们的大脑得以发展路径、建立连接，并最终学习语言。
由于你的宝宝在大脑发育的这个阶段不做梦，可以有把握地认为婴儿也不会做噩梦。噩梦源于创伤经历、过度活跃的想象力以及日常生活中的正常压力。
你是否想知道，婴儿梦见什么？好问题，但答案是什么都没有！那么，婴儿什么时候开始做梦？普遍的共识是他们在两岁左右开始做梦。心理学家David Foulkes研究儿童（从幼儿到青少年）以将他们梦境的秘密揭示出来。在他的实验室里，他让孩子们入睡，然后在夜间唤醒他们3次，让他们描述自己记得的内容。
Foulkes的发现并不令人惊讶。基本上，小孩子做小梦。但孩子们在做梦时看到的具体内容取决于他们的年龄。随着儿童的发育和成长，他们的梦境也在发展。

与成年人的梦境相比，幼儿的梦境通常只是快照，看起来更像幻灯片而不是电影。梦境中大量出现动物和其他熟悉的景象，比如人们吃东西的画面。根据Foulkes的说法，"儿童的梦境生活……似乎与他们清醒时的想象和叙述相似。"5至9岁的孩子开始看到移动的图像和活动中的人物。梦境现在包含一个接一个串联起来的多个事件。他们也开始发展出更强的记忆梦境的能力。不过，情况并非总是如此：在Foulkes的研究中，当在REM睡眠期间被唤醒时，25%的孩子不记得做过梦，这一趋势持续到9岁。
因此，如果你的宝宝在睡眠时似乎处于紧张状态或醒来时感到不安，可能还有其他因素在起作用。

passage:
New York's Eleven Madison Park has become the first vegan(素食主义的) restaurant to be awarded three Michelin stars.

The fine dining establishment received its first three-star Michelin rating in 2011 when the menu was famed for its fancy animal-based dishes.

However, last year, the restaurant's co-owner and famous chef, Daniel Humm, made the bold decision to remove meat from the menu, citing our unsustainable food system. While cow milk is still served for tea and coffee, the menu is almost 100 percent vegan.

At the time, Humm acknowledged the move was risky, admitting that "it wasn't clear if guests would come", but called the gamble "a risk worth taking."

"In view of the climate crisis, I didn't want to open the same restaurant," Humm told the Financial Times in an interview. "If we can show the possibilities of eating plant-based food in this setting, it can open a lot of doors" for others to follow.

Now, this impressive new accomplishment validates Eleven Madison Park's decision to take meat off the menu and embrace plant-based foods, with Michelin's 2022 New York guide branding it 'a bold vision of luxury dining'.

"We took the jump to transform Eleven Madison Park into a plant-based fine dining restaurant knowing in our hearts this is what we believed in," stated Humm on Instagram. "Last night, we were honored to be awarded three Michelin stars for the 11th year in a row. I am so grateful to the team members who contributed through its nearly 25-year history. We are also grateful to our guests and partners who believed in our vision and encouraged us to push harder."

Three Michelin stars is the highest award, given to chefs who are at the peak of their profession. "Their cooking is elevated to an art form and some of their dishes are destined to become classics," reads Michelin's website, in a clear nod to plant-based foods' growing significance in the culinary(烹饪的) world.

"I think luxury companies have a real role to play and a responsibility," says Humm. "The more creative we are, the more beautiful and delicious our future will be."
passage_translation: 纽约的Eleven Madison Park成为首家获得米其林三星的纯素餐厅。
这家高级餐厅于2011年首次获得米其林三星评级,当时菜单以其精致的动物性菜肴而闻名。
然而,去年,该餐厅的共同所有人兼著名厨师Daniel Humm做出了大胆决定,将肉类从菜单中移除,理由是我们不可持续的食物系统。虽然茶和咖啡仍然供应牛奶,但菜单几乎百分之百是纯素的。
当时,Humm承认此举有风险,他坦言"不清楚客人是否会来",但称这场赌博是"值得冒的风险"。
"鉴于气候危机,我不想开一家同样的餐厅,"Humm在接受《金融时报》采访时表示。"如果我们能在这种环境下展示植物性食物的可能性,就能为其他人效仿打开许多扇门。"
现在,这一令人瞩目的新成就证实了Eleven Madison Park将肉类从菜单中去除并拥抱植物性食物的决定是正确的,米其林2022年纽约指南将其誉为"奢华餐饮的大胆愿景"。
"我们大胆转型,将Eleven Madison Park打造成一家植物性高级餐厅,因为我们内心深知这是我们的信念所在,"Humm在Instagram上表示。"昨晚,我们荣幸地连续第11年获得米其林三星。我非常感谢在餐厅近25年历史中做出贡献的团队成员。我们也感谢相信我们愿景并鼓励我们更加努力的客人和合作伙伴。"
米其林三星是最高荣誉,授予处于职业巅峰的厨师。"他们的烹饪被提升为一种艺术形式,他们的一些菜肴注定会成为经典,"米其林网站如是说,这显然是对植物性食物在烹饪世界日益增长的重要性的认可。
"我认为奢侈品公司可以发挥真正的作用,也负有责任,"Humm说。"我们越有创造力,我们的未来就会越美好、越美味。"

passage:
With genetic testing becoming increasingly popular, many people are left wondering exactly how accurate it is. Whether you are taking a DNA test to build your extended DNA family tree, or want precise information on inborn(先天的) health conditions, it is important to understand how accurate genetic tests are, and what information we can rely upon.

How accurate DNA tests are relies greatly upon the kind of test being taken, on the specific question you ask, and on how complex the genetics behind a trait(特征) is. For example, tests for traits that depend on a single gene provide much more reliable results, because you can see whether a disease-causing trait is present.

Ancestry tests claim to reveal our genetic identities. But saying you are 30 percent East Asian or American hardly reflects your real ancestry.

What about using DNA tests to discover distant family members? There are tools to compare one's DNA with others' to find distant relatives based on their genetic identification. These kinds of applications are generally accurate. It's relatively easy to tell whether two DNA samples belong to close relatives. With distant relatives, results become hazier.

Genetic health tests claim to be able to detect certain hereditary(遗传的) diseases, or other health conditions. While certain rare diseases can be easily identified, most potential health conditions cannot be identified by genetic testing alone. The large majority of our traits and diseases also depend upon non-genetic factors, such as lifestyle, the environment, and many others.

Genetic tests for multi-factorial traits are often very tricky to interpret. Height, for example, depends on hundreds of genes, each contributing a little to the outcome, together with a bunch of environmental factors. A test can look at many genes at once, but it's difficult to predict how they will play together. Then you should also account for non-genetic factors that are not written in the DNA.

Tests that offer to find your perfect romantic match and those claiming to predict personality or talents based on your DNA are pure nonsense. At the moment, the scientific bases for these applications are non-existent or incredibly weak.
passage_translation: 随着基因检测越来越普及,许多人想知道它到底有多准确。无论你是进行DNA测试来构建你的扩展DNA家谱,还是想获得有关先天健康状况的精确信息,了解基因测试的准确程度以及我们可以依赖哪些信息都是很重要的。
DNA测试的准确程度在很大程度上取决于所进行的测试类型、你提出的具体问题以及特征背后遗传学的复杂程度。例如,依赖于单个基因的特征测试提供的结果要可靠得多,因为你可以看到是否存在致病特征。
祖源测试声称能揭示我们的基因身份。但说你是百分之三十的东亚人或美国人几乎不能反映你真正的祖源。
那么使用DNA测试来发现远房亲戚呢?有一些工具可以将一个人的DNA与其他人的DNA进行比较,以根据他们的基因识别找到远房亲戚。这类应用通常是准确的。判断两个DNA样本是否属于近亲是相对容易的。对于远房亲戚,结果就变得模糊了。
基因健康测试声称能够检测某些遗传性疾病或其他健康状况。虽然某些罕见疾病可以很容易地识别出来,但大多数潜在的健康状况无法仅通过基因测试来识别。我们的特征和疾病中的绝大多数还取决于非遗传因素,如生活方式、环境和许多其他因素。
多因素特征的基因测试通常很难解释。例如,身高取决于数百个基因,每个基因对结果的贡献都很小,再加上一系列环境因素。测试可以同时观察许多基因,但很难预测它们将如何共同发挥作用。然后你还应该考虑DNA中没有写入的非遗传因素。
那些提供寻找完美浪漫伴侣的测试以及那些声称根据你的DNA预测性格或天赋的测试都是纯粹的胡说八道。目前,这些应用的科学基础要么不存在,要么非常薄弱。

passage:
Is organic food worth the higher price? It's the classic grocery store dilemma. On the one hand, your family dinner table deserves only the best. On the other hand, your wallet can only stretch so far.

Whether or not to buy organic is a personal decision, said Mike von Massow, professor of Food Agriculture.

Science won't give a clear-cut answer to the question of whether organic food is "better". There are often trade-offs(权衡) and answers become less definitive depending on the product under consideration.

One thing is definitive: Organic and conventionally grown food are equally nutritious. From a nutrition point of view, there is no difference between organic and traditionally grown products.

Organic products don't necessarily have fewer pesticides(杀虫剂)—in fact, they may have more. There is also no big difference between organic and non-organic products from a food-safety perspective. Even organic growers use pesticides. Testing shows little if any pesticide remains on conventionally grown products.

In fact, organic farmers often use larger quantities of pesticide because they can only use the natural variety of insect-killers. Chemical pesticides generally kill a much wider range of pests(害虫) than any single natural pesticide.

The use of animal waste in organic agriculture can also be a factor in the spread of bacteria like E. coli and salmonella. Over the past 10 years, Canada has seen more food-safety recalls for organic products, proportionally, than for conventional products.

On the whole, organic agriculture may have a smaller environmental footprint. That's mostly because the risk of groundwater contamination from organic farming is lower. Organic farmers never use neonics, the controversial pesticides that have been linked to shrinking bee populations worldwide.

Traditional agriculture has been making "dramatic improvements" to reduce its impact on the environment.

It isn't a black-and-white picture, though.

Organic farming is much less efficient when it comes to land use, although yields vary considerably depending on the crop.

On the other hand, advocates of organic farming argue yields and efficiency could be significantly improved if the food industry devoted as much research and money to organic farming as it does conventional agriculture.
passage_translation: 有机食品是否值得更高的价格？这是杂货店购物时经典的两难选择。一方面，家人的餐桌只配得上最好的食物。另一方面，你的钱包也只能承受有限的开支。
食品与农业学教授迈克·冯·马索说，是否购买有机食品是个人的决定。
对于有机食品是否“更好”这个问题，科学无法给出明确的答案。这里面往往存在权衡，而且根据所考虑的产品不同，答案也会变得不那么确定。
有一点是确定的：有机食品和常规种植的食品营养价值相同。从营养角度看，有机产品与传统种植的产品之间没有差别。
有机产品未必含有更少的杀虫剂，事实上，它们所使用的杀虫剂可能更多。从食品安全角度看，有机产品与非有机产品之间也没有很大差别。即使是有机种植者也会使用杀虫剂。检测表明，常规种植的产品上残留的杀虫剂即使有，也非常少。
事实上，有机农民往往使用数量更多的杀虫剂，因为他们只能使用天然种类的杀虫剂。与任何一种天然杀虫剂相比，化学杀虫剂通常能够杀灭范围广得多的害虫。
在有机农业中使用动物排泄物，也可能成为大肠杆菌和沙门氏菌等细菌传播的一个因素。在过去10年里，加拿大有机产品被召回的食品安全事件占比高于常规产品。
总体而言，有机农业对环境的影响可能较小。这主要是因为有机农业造成地下水污染的风险较低。有机农民从不使用新烟碱类农药，而这种备受争议的杀虫剂一直被认为与全球蜜蜂数量减少有关。
传统农业一直在进行“显著的改进”，以减少其对环境的影响。
不过，情况并非非黑即白。
在土地利用方面，有机农业的效率低得多，尽管产量会因作物不同而有很大差异。
另一方面，有机农业的支持者认为，如果食品行业像投入常规农业那样投入同等多的研究和资金用于有机农业，那么产量和效率就可能得到显著提高。

passage:
It is still controversial whether we are fundamentally generous or selfish and whether these tendencies are shaped by our genes or environment.

Some evidence points to humans being born cooperative. At later stages in life we routinely work together to reach goals and help out in times of need.

Yet instances of selfish behavior are also plenty. One recent study tested people's willingness to set aside selfish interests to reach a greater good. It found that being selfish was more advantageous than cooperating. The benefit may be short-lived, however. Another study showed that players who cooperated did better in the long run.

It seems that human nature supports both pro-social and selfish traits(特征). Genetic studies have made some progress toward identifying their biological roots. By comparing identical twins, who share nearly 100 percent of their genes, and non-identical twins, who share about half, researchers have found overwhelming evidence for genetic effects on behaviors. In these twin studies, identical and non-identical twins are asked, for example, to split a sum of money with a peer. Such studies often also rely on careful psychological assessments and DNA analysis.

Other work highlights specific genes as key players. My colleagues and I recently identified a gene linked to altruistic(利他的) behavior and found that a particular variant of it was associated with more selfish behavior in preschoolers.

According to evolutionary scientists, cooperative behavior may have evolved first among relatives to promote the continuation of their genetic line. As communities diversified, mutual support could have broadened to include individuals not linked by blood. Another possibility is that humans cooperate to gain some advantage, such as boosting reputation. Finally, evolutionary processes take place at the group level. Groups of highly cooperative individuals have higher chances of survival because they can work together to reach goals that are unattainable to less cooperative groups.

Yet almost no behavior is entirely genetic, even among identical twins. Culture, schooling and parenting are important determinants of cooperation. Thus, the degree to which we act cooperatively or selfishly is unique to each individual and depends on a variety of genetic and environmental influences.
passage_translation: 关于我们从根本上说是慷慨还是自私，以及这些倾向是由我们的基因还是环境塑造的，目前仍存在争议。
一些证据表明，人类生来就具有合作倾向。在生命的后期阶段，我们通常会共同努力实现目标，并在他人有需要时提供帮助。
然而，自私行为的例子也比比皆是。最近的一项研究测试了人们为了实现更大的共同利益而搁置自私利益的意愿。研究发现，自私比合作更有利。不过，这种好处可能是短暂的。另一项研究表明，从长远来看，进行合作的参与者表现得更好。
看来，人性同时支持亲社会特征和自私特征。遗传学研究已经在确定这些特征的生物学根源方面取得了一些进展。通过比较基因几乎百分之百相同的同卵双胞胎和基因约有一半相同的异卵双胞胎，研究人员发现了行为受遗传因素影响的压倒性证据。在这些双胞胎研究中，研究人员会要求同卵双胞胎和异卵双胞胎，例如，将一笔钱分给一名同伴。这类研究通常还依赖于严谨的心理评估和DNA分析。
其他研究则强调了某些具体基因所发挥的关键作用。我的同事和我最近发现了一个与利他行为有关的基因，并发现该基因的某一特定变体与学龄前儿童更自私的行为有关。
根据进化科学家的观点，合作行为可能首先在亲属之间进化出来，以促进其遗传谱系的延续。随着群体日益多样化，相互支持可能扩大到包括没有血缘关系的个体。另一种可能性是，人类通过合作来获得某种优势，例如提升声誉。最后，进化过程也会发生在群体层面。高度合作的个体组成的群体具有更高的生存机会，因为他们能够共同实现那些合作程度较低的群体无法实现的目标。
然而，几乎没有任何行为完全由遗传决定，即使是在同卵双胞胎之间也是如此。文化、学校教育和父母养育方式都是影响合作的重要因素。因此，我们表现得合作或自私的程度因人而异，并取决于多种遗传和环境因素的影响。

passage:
People who systematically underestimate themselves and their own performance suffer from the so-called Impostor Phenomenon. They think that any success is due to external circumstances or just luck and chance. Those people live in constant fear that their "deception" will be exposed.

It is common for people to question their abilities now and again. A healthy amount of reflection and self-doubt can protect a person from acting impulsively. However, there are people who are permanently plagued by a massive amount of self-doubt despite delivering a good performance. They think that all of their successes are not a product of their skill or hard work, instead they attribute their own successes to external circumstances, for example, to luck and chance, or believe that their performance is massively overestimated by others. Failures, on the other hand, are always internalised as the result of their own shortcomings.

Psychologists from Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg examined the topic for the first time under real-life conditions. Seventy-six participants completed a range of intelligence tests and received positive feedback on them, regardless of their actual performance. They were then asked why they think they did so well.

The study showed two things: First, the self-reported degree of Impostor Phenomenon is not related to actual measured intelligence or performance. Secondly, the test supported the assumption that people with a tendency to exhibit the Impostor Phenomenon devalue their objectively measured performance and attribute positive results to external causes such as luck and chance, but not to their own abilities. These results are also completely unrelated to age and gender.

A permanent underestimation of one's own abilities is often accompanied by the fear that this supposed intellectual deception will be exposed sooner or later and that they will pay the price for this. The Impostor Phenomenon was first described in 1978 by US psychologists Pauline Clance and Suzanne Imes. They observed that there is a particularly high number of successful women who do not think they are very intelligent. The Impostor Phenomenon is not defined as a mental illness. However, people who suffer from it show a higher vulnerability to depression.
passage_translation: 系统性低估自己及自身表现的人会受到所谓的冒名顶替现象的困扰。他们认为，任何成功都归因于外部环境，或仅仅是运气和偶然。这些人始终生活在自己的“欺骗行为”会被揭穿的恐惧之中。
人们偶尔质疑自己的能力是很常见的。适度的反思和自我怀疑可以防止一个人冲动行事。然而，有些人尽管表现出色，却长期受到大量自我怀疑的困扰。他们认为，自己的所有成功都不是能力或努力的结果，而是将成功归因于外部环境，例如运气和偶然，或者认为自己的表现被他人严重高估。另一方面，他们总是把失败内化为自身缺点所导致的结果。
来自马丁·路德大学哈勒-维滕贝格分校的心理学家首次在现实生活条件下对这一主题进行了研究。76名参与者完成了一系列智力测试，并且无论其实际表现如何，都得到了积极的反馈。随后，研究人员询问他们为何认为自己表现得如此出色。
研究显示了两点：第一，自我报告的冒名顶替现象程度与实际测得的智力或表现无关。第二，测试支持了这一假设：倾向于表现出冒名顶替现象的人会贬低自己客观测得的表现，并将积极结果归因于运气和偶然等外部原因，而不是自己的能力。这些结果也与年龄和性别完全无关。
持续低估自己的能力，往往伴随着这样的恐惧：这种所谓的智力欺骗迟早会被揭穿，而他们也将为此付出代价。冒名顶替现象最早由美国心理学家保琳·克兰斯和苏珊·艾姆斯于1978年描述。她们观察到，成功女性中有相当多的人认为自己并不聪明。冒名顶替现象不被定义为一种精神疾病。然而，受到这一现象困扰的人表现出更高的抑郁易感性。

passage:
Music is a universal language. In every culture and country, you will find music. It is vitally important across the globe and has the potential to bring people together in peace and harmony. One of my favorite experiences in music is seeing musicians from different cultures come together and perform as a group. When each culture brings its own unique qualities to the group, an entirely new sound is achieved. This can create extraordinary results. People can communicate with each other using music as the common language.

One common musical thread between cultures is known as the pentatonic scale. It is astonishing how many cultures share this tool in approaching music. The pentatonic scale consists of five notes; "penta-" meaning 5, and "tonic" meaning tone or note. This scale can be found in music everywhere including that of Native Americans, Africans, and Asians. It is also found in popular music, blues, jazz, and rock. Using this five-note scale, musicians from around the globe have a medium through which they can relate, communicate, perform, and ultimately understand each other.

Music is tied to specific perceptual(感知的), mental, and emotional faculties, including language (all societies put words to their songs), motor control (people in all societies dance), sound analysis (all musical systems have a distinct pitch and quality), and aesthetics(美感) (their tunes and rhythms are balanced between repetitiveness and chaos).

There is no known society that existed without music. Although each culture has their own specific style and approach to music, you will find that the purposes behind music are very similar across the board. Music essentially serves to express or change emotions. It can cheer you up, sadden you, anger you or excite you. Music is often ceremonial: used in religion, ceremony, and celebration. Music can simply be recreational: entertaining, joyful and fun. Any way you have used music, it is almost certain that every other culture has used music in the very same way. And that is something that bonds all of us. We all share a deep love for music and it has the power to unite us.
passage_translation: 音乐是一种通用语言。在每一种文化和每一个国家中，你都能找到音乐。音乐在全球范围内都极其重要，并且有可能以和平与和谐将人们团结在一起。我在音乐方面最喜欢的经历之一，就是看到来自不同文化的音乐家聚在一起，以一个团体的形式进行演奏。当每种文化都为这个团体带来自身独特的特质时，便会产生一种全新的声音。这可以创造出非凡的成果。人们可以用音乐作为共同语言彼此交流。
不同文化之间一个共同的音乐纽带被称为五声音阶。令人惊叹的是，有如此多的文化都采用这一音乐工具。五声音阶由五个音组成；“penta-”意为“5”，“tonic”意为“音调”或“音符”。这种音阶遍布各地的音乐之中，包括美洲原住民、非洲人和亚洲人的音乐。流行音乐、蓝调、爵士乐和摇滚乐中也能找到它。借助这一五声音阶，来自世界各地的音乐家拥有了一种媒介，使他们能够相互联系、交流、演奏，并最终彼此理解。
音乐与特定的感知、心理和情感能力密切相关，包括语言能力（所有社会都会为歌曲配上歌词）、运动控制能力（所有社会中的人都会跳舞）、声音分析能力（所有音乐体系都有独特的音高和音质）以及美感（它们的曲调和节奏在重复与混乱之间保持平衡）。

没有已知的社会是在没有音乐的情况下存在的。尽管每种文化都有自己独特的音乐风格和处理方式，但你会发现，音乐背后的目的在各个文化中大同小异。音乐本质上是用来表达或改变情感的。它可以让你振奋、使你悲伤、让你愤怒或使你兴奋。音乐常常具有仪式性：用于宗教活动、仪式和庆祝活动。音乐也可以仅仅用于娱乐：带来消遣、欢乐和乐趣。无论你以何种方式使用音乐，几乎可以肯定，其他每种文化也都以完全相同的方式使用过音乐。而这正是将我们所有人联系在一起的事物。我们都对音乐怀有深厚的热爱，而音乐拥有将我们团结起来的力量。

passage:
Disgust is a universal human emotion. One type of disgust is called physical disgust, which protects us from eating or touching things that could be dangerous for us, such as raw meat or insects. Children experience physical disgust from a very early age, but do not achieve an understanding of the concept until they are around four years old.

Some researchers maintain that there is another type of disgust, called moral disgust, that protects us from engaging in activities that can be perceived as morally wrong. Examples of moral disgust are stealing, lying or cheating.

However, not all academics think that moral disgust really exists. Some say that when we refer to disgust in relation to moral issues, we are using disgust as a metaphor(隐喻), and what we are feeling is in reality anger.

If moral disgust appears quite late in development, it makes sense to think that there is actually a social component to it. Children learn about emotions in many different ways. Of special relevance are parents-children conversations about emotions. Indeed, children whose parents talk about emotions often have a better emotional understanding than children whose parents do not discuss emotions often.

However, there are no studies that have examined how parents and children talk about disgust. This is what we set up to examine in our study.

We asked 68 English-speaking mothers and their four-, six- or eight-year-old children to discuss some stories about moral and physical disgust. Our preliminary findings show mothers and children do talk about disgust, but mainly about physical disgust and not so much about moral disgust.

When we asked mothers and children to discuss moral issues, such as whether it is OK to play with a child who has stolen someone else's snack, they linked this type of moral wrongdoing with the emotion of anger and not disgust.

Does this mean that moral disgust does not exist? Some researchers suggest moral disgust exists in adults. Our findings suggest that moral disgust is either understood at a later age or is only used metaphorically, if at all, in children as old as eight years.
passage_translation: 厌恶是一种普遍存在于人类身上的情绪。厌恶有一种类型被称为生理性厌恶，它保护我们不去食用或触摸可能对我们有害的东西，例如生肉或昆虫。儿童从很小的时候就会产生生理性厌恶，但直到大约四岁时才会理解这一概念。
一些研究人员认为，厌恶还有另一种类型，即道德性厌恶，它保护我们不参与那些可能被视为道德错误的活动。道德性厌恶的例子包括偷窃、撒谎或作弊。
然而，并非所有学者都认为道德性厌恶确实存在。有些人说，当我们将厌恶与道德问题联系起来时，我们是在把厌恶当作隐喻，而实际上我们感受到的是愤怒。
如果道德性厌恶在发展过程中出现得相当晚，那么认为它实际上包含社会因素就是合理的。儿童通过许多不同的方式了解情绪。其中尤其相关的是亲子之间关于情绪的谈话。事实上，父母经常谈论情绪的儿童，其情绪理解能力通常优于父母不常讨论情绪的儿童。
然而，还没有研究考察过父母和儿童是如何谈论厌恶的。这正是我们在研究中着手考察的问题。
我们邀请了68位讲英语的母亲及其四岁、六岁或八岁的孩子，让他们讨论一些有关道德性厌恶和生理性厌恶的故事。我们的初步研究结果表明，母亲和孩子确实会谈论厌恶，但主要谈论的是生理性厌恶，而较少谈论道德性厌恶。
当我们让母亲和孩子讨论道德问题时，例如与偷了别人的零食的孩子一起玩是否可以，他们把这种道德错误与愤怒这种情绪联系起来，而不是与厌恶联系起来。
这是否意味着道德性厌恶并不存在？一些研究人员认为，成年人存在道德性厌恶。我们的研究结果表明，八岁及以下的儿童要么在更晚的年龄才理解道德性厌恶，要么根本不使用道德性厌恶，即使使用，也只是将其作为隐喻。

passage:
After finding out details about a stranger, we mistakenly think that they also know about us. As a result, we act more honestly around them, according to a recent study in Nature.

Past research has found that we tend to assume social relationships are reciprocal(相互的). Most of the time, this assumption is accurate: someone you think of as a friend will usually consider you a friend too. But sometimes our social ties are more one-sided: for example, you might learn something about a stranger who doesn't know you at all. Researchers Anuj Shah and Michael LaForest wondered whether our tendency to believe that social ties are reciprocal could lead us to mistakenly feel that a stranger does actually know us.

In a series of lab-based studies, this is exactly what the researchers found. When we know about strangers, we erroneously think they also know about us. But the really interesting finding came when the researchers stepped out of the lab, to conduct a field experiment. The team developed leaflets(传单) containing fairly ordinary information about local community police officers, such as their favourite food, hobbies, or reasons for joining the police force. They then sent out these leaflets to every apartment in a number of housing developments in disadvantaged areas. The officers themselves also dropped off cards to local residents containing similar information.

Two months later, the researchers surveyed residents at these housing developments as well as control areas that did not receive leaflets or outreach cards. Residents were asked to imagine that they had committed a crime and how likely it would be that local officers would find out about it. They also rated how well the officers in the area knew them.

The team found that residents of the developments that had received the leaflets believed it more likely that local officers would find out about illegal activity than residents of the control areas. Even more strikingly, the team found that immediately after the leaflet distribution, there were fewer criminal complaints and arrests in the areas around the developments that had received the leaflets than around the control developments.
passage_translation: 《自然》杂志近期发表的一项研究显示，在了解到陌生人的一些情况后，我们会错误地认为对方也了解我们。因此，我们在他们面前会表现得更加诚实。
以往的研究发现，我们往往认为社会关系是相互的。大多数时候，这一假设是准确的：你认为是朋友的人通常也会把你当作朋友。但有时我们的社会关系更具单向性：例如，你可能了解到一个完全不认识你的陌生人的一些情况。研究人员阿努杰·沙阿和迈克尔·拉福里斯特想知道，我们相信社会关系具有相互性的倾向，是否会导致我们错误地觉得陌生人确实了解我们。
研究人员通过一系列实验室研究发现，事实正是如此。当我们了解到陌生人的一些情况时，会错误地认为他们也了解我们。但真正有趣的发现出现在研究人员走出实验室进行一项实地实验之后。研究团队制作了一些传单，内容是当地社区警察的较为普通的信息，例如他们最喜欢的食物、兴趣爱好或加入警察队伍的原因。随后，他们将这些传单发放到不发达地区若干住宅小区的每一套公寓。警察本人也向当地居民发放了载有类似信息的卡片。
两个月后，研究人员对这些住宅小区的居民以及未收到传单或宣传卡片的对照区域居民进行了调查。研究人员要求居民设想自己实施了一项犯罪，并评估当地警察发现这件事的可能性有多大。他们还对当地警察对自己的了解程度进行了评价。
研究团队发现，收到传单的住宅小区居民认为当地警察发现违法活动的可能性高于对照区域的居民。更令人惊讶的是，研究团队发现，在传单发放后不久，收到传单的住宅小区周边地区的犯罪报案数和逮捕人数都少于对照小区周边地区。
